refreshes.scope: Retention measurement and programme under PenniLogic/docs#8: the activation funnel and week-one and week-four cohorts (android#7), the retention programme with milestones, digests, dormancy re-engagement and its kill criterion (android#38), server-side experiment assignment and exposure logging (api#63), the debt-first concept test (docs#53, Sprint 01) and moderated usability of the onboarding and permission prototype (docs#54). The threat surface is the analytics pipeline (event payloads, pseudonymous identifiers, opt-out, the dashboard the team reads), experiment assignment and exposure integrity, retention messaging that surfaces debt status outside the app, and the participants of the two studies. The epic's own exit criteria already forbid financial values in any analytics payload; this refresh records the controls that make that provable and the gaps around them.
sources: product/02-risk-register.md (R2 retention, privacy leakage through analytics)
PenniLogic/docs#8 (epic body: scope, out of scope, exit criteria, key risks)

categories.analysis: Analytics identities are pseudonymous, so spoofing here means a client claiming another identity's events or a treatment it was not assigned. Server-side assignment and server-stamped exposure logging (E07-F04) are the control; a client-chosen identifier or self-reported assignment would let one device manufacture another cohort's behaviour.
evidence: architecture/02-security-architecture.md#8-privacy-engineering: analytics identifiers are a keyed hash of the user identifier, unlinkable without the pepper

categories.analysis: The retention signal decides whether the product continues, so the integrity of events, assignments and cohorts is the asset. Two gaps: assignment and exposure must be server-side and append-only rather than client-reported (E07-F04), and event ingestion, the pipeline and the dashboard the team reads have no owning ticket for schema validation, rate limits and deduplication, so forged or inflated events from a rooted device or a script would be counted (E07-F05).

Opt-out must be provable and effective: a user who opted out and later sees their behaviour in a cohort has a valid dispute. The control is a server-side record in the consent ledger that assignment and exposure logging consult, not a client flag alone (E07-F03).
evidence: PenniLogic/api#24: consent ledger, purpose registry and data-principal rights

categories.analysis: Three channels leak debt status. Event payloads: the exit criterion forbids financial values, but derived values such as payoff horizon, debt count or milestone are quasi-financial and need coarsening, and the allowlist needs a test rather than a code review (E07-F01). Retention messages: a digest or dormancy nudge puts a balance or a debt-free date on a lock screen, an email preview or a widget where a household member reads it (E07-F02). Study participants: the concept test and usability sessions gather personal financial disclosures under the research evidence system (E07-F06). Dashboards over small cohorts are part of the unowned pipeline (E07-F05).
evidence: PenniLogic/docs#8 exit criteria: zero financial values in any analytics payload, verified by inspecting captured events
PenniLogic/android#16: automated privacy traffic inspection on every release candidate (E25)

categories.analysis: An event flood from one device or script inflates ingestion cost and buries real signal; without per-device rate limits and deduplication in the pipeline the same unowned gap as E07-F05 applies.

No privileged operation is introduced: analytics events are write-only from the client, assignment is read-only for the client, and access to aggregate views belongs to the admin console (E13, admin#7), which its own refresh reviews.
No payment or entitlement path is touched. Retention messaging about plans is designed in docs#98 (E35) and billing itself in E14.

No entitlement state is read or written; experiment assignment is not an entitlement and must not gate paid features (a treatment that unlocks a paid feature would be an entitlement path and a scope_changed trigger for this record).

No model, gateway or provider key is used; digests and milestones are template-driven. Generating digest text with a model would be a scope_changed trigger and would bring prompt injection through merchant names into scope.
The clients are native applications posting to first-party endpoints; no browser session is exposed and no supplied URL is fetched. Forged event posts are a tampering concern (E07-F05).
No model reads untrusted content in this epic; see the ai_service_compromise note on template-driven digests.
No shared ledger or settlement is involved; retention events about split features, when E15 exists, must follow the same allowlist as every other event.

The epic introduces no operator identity. Whoever administers the analytics dashboard is part of the unowned pipeline gap (E07-F05) and, once the dashboard has an owner, of the admin console's operator model (E13).

findings.title: The event allowlist must be a tested schema and must coarsen derived debt values
findings.attack_path: An event carries an amount, balance, merchant name, account reference or a precise derived value such as a payoff date or debt count; it leaves the device and is stored in the analytics pipeline, where it re-identifies financial status even though no raw amount was sent.
findings.recommended_control: An allowlisted event schema enforced by a unit test that fails on any unknown property; derived values emitted only as coarse bands; identifiers as a keyed hash with a server-held pepper; captured release-candidate traffic inspected against the same schema (android#16).

findings.title: Digests, milestones and dormancy nudges can expose debt status outside the app
findings.attack_path: A progress digest, milestone or re-engagement message shows a balance, a debt-free date or the word debt on a lock screen, in an email subject or preview, or in a widget, where a family member, colleague or abuser reads it.
findings.recommended_control: Message content chosen server-side from an allowlist with no financial values or debt words in any surface shown outside the unlocked app; privacy mode honoured; user-controlled channel and content preferences; the retention programme's kill criterion measured without exposing the value that triggered the message.

findings.title: Analytics opt-out must be recorded and enforced server-side
findings.attack_path: A user opts out on one device; the flag lives only in that client, a second device or a reinstall keeps reporting, and exposure logging continues on the server, so the user's dispute is valid and the product cannot show when opt-out took effect.
findings.recommended_control: Opt-out written to the consent ledger with a timestamp; assignment and exposure logging consult it on every request and stop; clients treat the server state as authoritative; a test proves an opted-out identity produces no exposure rows.

findings.title: Experiment assignment and exposure must be server-side and append-only
findings.attack_path: A client reports its own treatment or posts exposure events for a treatment it never saw; a rooted device or script shifts cohort behaviour and the holdout comparison that drives the kill decision.
findings.recommended_control: Deterministic server-side assignment returned to the client, exposure rows written by the server with its own timestamp, no client-supplied assignment or exposure accepted, and rows never updated or deleted.

findings.title: Event ingestion, the pipeline and the team dashboard have no owning ticket
findings.attack_path: Forged, replayed or flooded events from a rooted device or a script are accepted without schema validation, per-device rate limits or deduplication; the retention signal that decides whether the debt-first wedge continues is corrupted, ingestion cost rises, and a dashboard over a small cohort re-identifies users.
findings.recommended_control: An owning ticket for the ingestion endpoint and pipeline: schema validation against the E07-F01 allowlist, per-identity rate limits and deduplication, append-only storage with retention, a dashboard with cohort minimums and a named access list, and no third-party analytics SDK on the client.

findings.title: Concept-test and usability participants fall under the research evidence system
findings.attack_path: Recordings and notes from the debt-first concept test or the onboarding usability sessions, which include personal debt disclosures, are stored or quoted outside the participant-data rules because the studies sit in this epic rather than in E33.
findings.recommended_control: Both studies run under the participant evidence system: classification, storage and access list, consent and withdrawal records, pseudonymised quotes, retention and erasure, and no raw artifact in a repository, issue or prompt (the same controls as E33-F01 and E33-F02).
